full_judgment:
This appeal arises out of a suit for declaration of title and khas possession. 

 4. Both parties adduced oral and documentary evidence in support of their respective cases. Upon a consideration of the same, the learned Munsif found that Matangini was dead and the plaintiffs were the reversionary heirs of her deceased husband and found plaintiff's title in respect of plot No. 5882 and allowed khas possession of the same but dismissed the suit in respect of plots Nos. 5647 and 5883 on the ground that the transfer of Matangini to her father Tenu Mondal was for legal necessity. On appeal by the plaintiffs, the learned Subordinate Judge set aside the judgment of the trial court and decreed the plaintiffs suit in full after declaring the plaintiffs title to the entire suit lands and also allowed them to get khas possession. The defendants however preferred a second appeal before this Court which was allowed and the appeal was sent back on remand for rehearing on the point as to whether Matangini had legal necessity to transfer the suit lands. The learned Subordinate Judge thereafter reheard the appeal and dismissed it and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. Hence the present appeal at the instance of the plaintiffs.
